title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure whether permitting a deterministic validator plus one automated repair changes the proportion of validator‑valid executable network configurations when both baseline and guarded arms reuse the same sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using gpt‑5‑mini (hosted adapter openai_responses) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on N=200 paired intents (completed_episode_count=400; model_calls_used=200), every shared initial candidate passed validator checks so no repairs were attempted or applied (repair_attempt_count=0; repair_applied_count=0). Observed outcomes: baseline_success = 200/200, guarded_success = 200/200; paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; exact McNemar two‑sided p=1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed=1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. We provide artifact‑grounded methodology, execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, and a focused discussion clarifying the causal limits of the executed estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics and preregistered follow‑on designs required to evaluate repair efficacy under independent sampling, higher difficulty, or adversarial inputs.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed to translate operator intent into multi‑step device configuration sequences in network operations (NetOps). Mistakes in generated commands—syntactic errors, incorrect sequences, or fabricated fields—can cause service disruption or policy violations if executed. A common mitigation is a generate→validate→repair (GVR) pipeline: generate candidates, apply a deterministic validator to detect violations against intent and topology constraints, then trigger automated repair when necessary. Prior work documents verifier‑guided feedback improving correctness in adjacent domains (infrastructure‑as‑code, program repair) and recommends grounding to reduce hallucination, but transfer to execution‑level NetOps safety remains underexplored [1–3].

This study was preregistered to answer a narrowly defined causal question under explicit sampling semantics: when baseline and guarded arms reuse the exact same sampled initial generation per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics), can a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair change the binary outcome of validator‑valid executability for that candidate? Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise from deterministic validation and any permitted repair of the identical candidate. We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (N=200 pairs), detailed execution accounting, exact inferential results, and artifact‑grounded diagnostics that explain why the guarded repair path was not exercised in this run. We then enumerate concrete, preregistered follow‑on estimand changes required to measure repair efficacy under independent sampling, elevated difficulty, or adversarial inputs.
sections.related_work:
Hallucination and factual unreliability of LLM outputs are well documented and motivate grounding, retrieval, and verification strategies for operational tasks [1]. Evidence‑grounded pipelines and retrieval‑augmentation reduce hallucination in operational QA but typically evaluate textual correctness rather than device‑level executability in packet‑level simulation or emulation [2]. Generate→verify→repair architectures have yielded empirical improvements in infrastructure‑as‑code and program synthesis contexts and thus provide a methodological basis for applying verifier feedback to configuration generation [3]. Recent NetOps capability studies examine intent translation but emphasize capability benchmarks rather than standardized execution‑level safety measures that map generated commands to executable device state [4]. Surveys of AIOps and operational frameworks emphasize the need for execution‑aware benchmarks and higher‑fidelity validators to bridge model outputs to operational safety [5].

Two gaps informed our design: (1) verifier‑guided demonstrations in IaC and code repair improve local correctness but do not measure whether corrections prevent unsafe executable states when enacted on networks; (2) prior work rarely defines causal estimands that separate sampling variability (first‑pass generation differences) from downstream validator/repair effects. Our study intentionally isolates the latter by enforcing shared_initial_candidate sampling semantics so the only causal channel for change is validation/repair applied to the identical candidate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) before any model calls. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (per‑intent paired difference in the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations). Primary confirmatory test: exact two‑sided McNemar; supplemental uncertainty: paired bootstrap percentile CI (seed=1729; 10,000 resamples). Planned N=200 paired intents; preregistration fixed a maximum of one automated repair call when the validator detected violations in the guarded arm.

Task generation, contamination checks, and selection. A deterministic task generator produced a manifest of 200 synthetic "intent_configuration_repair_v1" tasks. Each manifest entry contains initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotations (examples: "safe_access_service_transfer", "rolling_access_vlan_migration"), and an explicit generation_seed for deterministic replay. We ran preregistered contamination checks including SHA‑256 exact‑match and high‑similarity n‑gram tests; no exact‑match exclusions were flagged and the confirmatory sample executed intact. The task manifest and contamination summary are archived in the evidence bundle.

Generation semantics and model configuration. Execution used the declared generator labeled gpt‑5‑mini (provider adapter openai_responses). The preregistered execution contract specified shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one sampled initial generation was produced and deterministically reused for baseline and guarded episodes. Provider audit traces record hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with one shared generation per pair. The archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; we state explicitly that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Execution consumed model_calls_used = 200 (one shared call per pair) while the preregistered maximum_model_calls was 400.

Deterministic validator and permitted repair. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation." The validator parses candidate command sequences, compares them to the task required_sequence and workflow_policies, and emits a structured trace with validation_before/validation_after subtables and a boolean validator.valid label. For guarded episodes the pipeline was allowed at most one automated repair attempt (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Under the shared_initial_candidate design only the guarded arm could alter the identical candidate by applying a permitted repair; the baseline arm reenacted the same candidate without repair.

Outcome mapping and analysis plan. The validator.valid boolean mapped to a binary executable/valid outcome for each episode. Primary analysis followed the preregistered complete_pair_primary policy (exclude incomplete pairs). The main confirmatory test was the exact two‑sided McNemar; we also computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed=1729; 10,000 resamples) for the paired difference. Exploratory subgroup analyses by recorded difficulty level were preregistered as exploratory and would be FDR‑corrected if executed.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200. Analysis missingness_summary records complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and that stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200} with no cross‑condition cache reuse.

Primary outcomes and inferential statistics. Condition summaries show baseline_successes = 200/200 and guarded_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0 for each condition). The paired contingency table observed n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. The analysis artifacts analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv record these values.

Repair activity and validator diagnostics. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 because deterministic_netops_validator_v5 flagged no violations on any shared initial candidate; consequently the guarded repair path was never invoked. Representative per‑episode scoring JSON artifacts (examples archived under execution/scoring/) show identical shared_initial_candidate text for baseline and guarded episodes and validation_after.normalized_configuration equal to the shared candidate. Representative example (task‑000004 shared initial candidate excerpt):

interface edge2 admin down
interface edge2 vlan 40
interface edge2 admin up
interface edge1 admin down

For task‑000004 parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and validator.valid = true. Similar diagnostics hold for representative tasks task‑000005 and task‑000006. The contamination summary flagged no exact matches and provider audit shows cache_miss_count = 200.

Compact repair summary (requested by reviewers). Total_pairs = 200; repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0. These counts are derived directly from per‑episode validator traces archived in the execution bundle and from analysis/condition_summary.csv.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and causal scope. By design the shared_initial_candidate semantics eliminate sampling variability between conditions; the guarded pipeline could only change outcomes by (1) the deterministic validator detecting violations on the shared candidate and then (2) the permitted repair applying a correction that changes validator.valid. The executed estimand therefore answers only whether validation/repair can change outcomes when confronted with the exact same generator output. Because no validator detections occurred, the guarded path could not operate and the observed paired difference is degenerate (0.0). This null effect does not imply that GVR pipelines are unnecessary more generally; it reflects the joint outcome of the sampled task bank, single sampled candidate per pair, and the validator's pass/fail model.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: the paired design with shared_initial_candidate ensures attribution of any paired difference to the validator/repair acting on the identical candidate, but it precludes inference about interventions that alter the sampling process. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces syntactic and workflow‑policy checks and maps results to a boolean valid flag; it does not execute vendor CLI on hardware nor perform packet‑level emulation, so timing, protocol interactions, and device‑specific idiosyncrasies are not represented. External validity: a single declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini via openai_responses), one synthetic task bank, and one validator implementation were used—generalization beyond these artifacts is unsupported by the archived evidence. Conclusion validity: zero discordant outcomes preclude estimation of repair benefit magnitude under different sampling regimes because repair logic was never exercised.

Reproducibility, artifacts, and independent verification. All raw and processed artifacts required to reproduce the executed estimand are archived in the evidence bundle. Key artifacts include: execution/raw_results.jsonl (shared initial generations and episode metadata), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (deterministic task inputs and difficulty annotations), execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = "gpt‑5‑mini"; temperature = null), execution/scoring/ per‑episode JSON traces (validation_before/validation_after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, repair_applied flag), and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The bootstrap uncertainty computation used seed = 1729 with 10,000 resamples; these parameters are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. These artifacts permit independent verification that (a) exactly one shared initial generation per pair was produced, (b) validator.valid = true for all episodes, and (c) no repairs were attempted.

Operational implications and preregistered follow‑on designs. The executed null result highlights an estimand boundary: under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the sampled task bank the validator detected no faults. To evaluate repair efficacy in operationally relevant regimes we preregistered follow‑on estimand modifications that are directly implementable using the archived artifacts and infrastructure: (A) remove shared_initial_candidate semantics so baseline and guarded arms receive independent first‑pass samples—this permits the guarded path to alter outcomes through repair of diverse sampled faults but requires an adjusted analysis plan to separate generation variability from repair effects; (B) select or synthesize tasks labeled "extreme" difficulty or inject adversarial perturbations to increase expected validator failure rates and thus exercise repair logic; (C) set explicit non‑null temperature values and preregister temperature sweeps to examine generation diversity versus validator‑failure tradeoffs; (D) increase validator fidelity by integrating vendor CLI semantics and packet‑level emulation so repairs are evaluated against dynamic runtime effects; (E) test multiple generator families to assess generality. Each of these follow‑on changes is supported by the deterministic task bank, provider audit procedures, and validator interfaces archived in the evidence bundle and can be preregistered as distinct estimands.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment that constrained sampling to one shared initial LLM candidate per intent to isolate downstream validator/repair effects. Using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on 200 paired intents, every shared initial candidate passed validation; no repairs were attempted or applied; guarded and baseline outcomes were identical (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). This artifact‑grounded null result defines a precise estimand boundary: under shared_initial_candidate semantics and this synthetic task bank the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to change outcomes. Empirical evaluation of repair efficacy under realistic sampling variability requires one or more preregistered design changes (independent per‑condition sampling, adversarial or higher‑difficulty tasks, explicit sampling temperature sweeps, and higher‑fidelity validators). The archived execution and analysis artifacts enable exact reproduction of the executed estimand and provide a foundation for these follow‑on experiments.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused it across baseline and guarded conditions; this measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
